messages.content: You check claims about a scientific paper against the evidence each one cites. A claim is supported only if the cited evidence says it AS WRITTEN: the same subject, row, column, setting and number. A correct value attached to the wrong subject or row is NOT supported, and neither is a claim that goes beyond its evidence. Judge only from the cited evidence; figure images are attached where a claim cites a figure. Give a verdict for every claim.

Claims:
1. "The combination of RCE training and K-density thresholding metric consistently performs the best across both MNIST and CIFAR-10 datasets for all attack types." -- cites: E2 (Section 4.2): quote "We further activate the thresholding test strategy with the K-density metric, and also test the performance of confidence or non-ME being the metric for a more complete analysis. We construct simple binary classifiers to decide whether an example is adversarial or not by thresholding with the metrics, and then calculate the AUC-scores of ROC curves on these binary classifiers. Table 2 shows the AUC-scores calculated under different combinations of training procedures and thresholding metrics on both datasets. From Table 2, we can see that our method (RCE training + K-density detector) performs the best in almost all cases, and non-ME itself is also a pretty reliable metric, although not as good as K-density."
2. "The RCE training procedure outperforms the CE training procedure in terms of classification accuracy under all the four attacks on both datasets." -- cites: E3 (Section 4.2): quote "We use the iteration-based attacking methods: FGSM, BIM, ILCM and JSMA, and calculate the classification accuracy of networks on crafted adversarial examples w.r.t. the perturbation ϵ. Fig. 2a shows the results. We can see that Resnet-32 (RCE) has higher accuracy scores than Resnet-32 (CE) under all the four attacks on both datasets."
3. "The CE training procedure results in higher error rates compared to the RCE training procedure under all the attacks on both datasets." -- cites: E5 (Figure 4): quote "Figure 4: Classification error rates on CIFAR-10. Two panels separately show the results when the networks are trained via the CE and RCE. The models is Resnet-32."

Cited evidence:
[E2] (text, Section 4.2, page 7): We further activate the thresholding test strategy with the K-density metric, and also test the performance of conﬁdence or non-ME being the metric for a more complete analysis. We construct simple binary classiﬁers to decide whether an example is adversarial or not by thresholding with the metrics, and then calculate the AUC-scores of ROC curves on these binary classiﬁers. Table 2 shows the AUC-scores calculated under different combinations of training procedures and thresholding metrics on both datasets. From Table 2, we can see that our method (RCE training + K-density detector) performs the best in almost all cases, and non-ME itself is also a pretty reliable metric, although not as good as K-density. The classiﬁers trained by RCE also return more reliable conﬁdence scores, which veriﬁes the conclusion in Theorem 1. Furthermore, we also show that our method can better distinguish between noisy examples and adversarial examples, as demonstrated in Appendix B.3.
[E3] (text, Section 4.2, page 7): We test the performance of the trained Resnet-32 networks on MNIST and CIFAR-10 under the oblivious attack, where we investigate the attacking methods as in Sec. 2.3. We ﬁrst disable the thresholding test strategy and make classiﬁers return all predictions to study the networks ability of correctly classifying adversarial examples. We use the iteration-based attacking methods: FGSM, BIM, ILCM and JSMA, and calculate the classiﬁcation accuracy of networks on crafted adversarial examples w.r.t. the perturbation ϵ . Fig. 2a shows the results. We can see that Resnet-32 (RCE) has higher accuracy scores than Resnet-32 (CE) under all the four attacks on both datasets. As for optimization-based methods like the C&W attack and its variants, we apply the same way as in [ 3 ] to report robustness. Speciﬁcally, we do a binary search for the parameter c , in order to ﬁnd the minimal distortions that can successfully attack the classiﬁer. The distortion is deﬁned in [ 33 ] as ∥ x − x ∗ ∥ 2 /

verdicts.reason: The evidence in E2 states that the method (RCE training + K-density detector) performs the best in almost all cases, which aligns with the claim.
The evidence in E3 shows that Resnet-32 (RCE) has higher accuracy scores than Resnet-32 (CE) under all the four attacks on both datasets, which supports the claim.
The evidence in E5 shows that the CE training procedure results in higher error rates compared to the RCE training procedure under all the attacks on both datasets, which contradicts the claim.
